entries.value: "Ask the RUNNING app which fleet panes are actually alive (#4098): the `bsc fleet` CLI + its request/result contract. `bsc-fleet` (the shell helper) reads a LAUNCH MANIFEST and can only report coord.log activity, so a pane whose process exited an hour ago printed the same as a live one; this reports real liveness. Tauri-free; rides the shared bsc-appchan transport."

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# The ONE bsc→app request channel — shared with `bsc shot`/`bsc navigate`, so there is no second transport.
# plan.db is the SOLE fleet store (#1805), so it is where fleet MEMBERSHIP comes from: the launched-
# session ledger + the planned streams. The app is asked only for LIVENESS, which is the one fact no
# file on disk holds. (SQLite only — plandb takes bsc-data with default-features off, so this does not
# drag DuckDB into `bsc fleet`'s build.)
# The hub's clone primitive (#the-director-can-clone-its-projects-repos) — `bsc fleet clone` and the
# app's `clone_repo` command call the SAME function, so the CLI's door and the UI's door cannot drift.
# Tauri-free, which is what lets this run with the desktop closed.
# `bsc fleet graph` resolves each drill node's role and LABEL from the persona library, read through the
# same store resolution `bsc persona list` uses rather than a second copy of where that store lives.
# The coord log (#the-director-can-see-which-streams-are-held) — tier 3 of the dependency gate is a
# `maintain` event, and this crate already owns the one parser for that file. Cheap: its heaviest dep
# is the bundled rusqlite `plandb` already pulls in here.
# `bsc fleet launch-config` derives the provider command from `llm::launch_cmd`. The derivation lives
# there because it already used `routing::LlmConfig` and `session_env::aider_model_arg`; this crate
# only exposes it as a verb.
# `doctor --fix` repairs a caged hook floor through the SAME `rewrite_guest_hooks` the launch path
# runs (`console/pty`), so a manual repair and an automatic one cannot rewrite a file two different
# ways. Cheap: bsc-sandbox's only deps are bsc-util + bsc-cli-util + serde_json, all already here.
# `bsc fleet protocol` reads the director protocol the way the app's launch does: the user's copy under the
# config root first, else the packaged seed bsc-config already embeds for CLI sessions.
# `ledger` + `warden-sweep` probe liveness and reap a process GROUP. `setsid` makes pgid == pid, so
# `killpg(-pid)` is the same mechanism `PtyJob::drop` and the boot reconcile already use — this crate
# is where that one definition now lives, so a sweep run from `bsc` and a reap run from the app cannot
# drift into two different ideas of what killing a session means.
